implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__ creates a size×size grid with default size=15 (board.py, line 12‑15). Main launches Game with board_size=15 (main.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing black and white stones
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.current_player starts as Board.BLACK and is switched after each successful move (Game.switch_player, game.py). GUI passes the current player to the preview stone (gui.py, on_hover).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Move validation (inside board and empty cell)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move checks bounds and emptiness (board.py, line 22‑24). Game.handle_move rejects invalid moves (game.py, line 31‑33).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Win detection for five in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win scans four directions and returns a line when length >=5 (board.py, line 38‑55). Game.handle_move uses this to set STATE_WON (game.py, line 38‑45).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full iterates over rows to detect a full board (board.py, line 28‑33). Game.handle_move sets STATE_DRAW if is_full() returns true (game.py, line 46‑48).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical interface showing board, stones, turn status, and win highlighting
implemented_requirements.evidence: GomokuGUI draws grid, stones, and highlights winning_line (gui.py, draw_board). It updates a status label with Game.get_status_text (gui.py, line 21‑23).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to start a new game
implemented_requirements.evidence: GUI button calls reset_game which invokes Game.reset (gui.py, reset_game).

critical_issues: None observed that prevent core functionality. Minor cosmetic issues (e.g., line sorting in check_win) do not affect gameplay.
judge.summary: The submitted files provide a complete, functional Gomoku implementation on a 15x15 board with alternating black/white turns, proper move validation, win/draw detection, and a Tkinter GUI that displays the board, stones, turn status, and highlights the winning line. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run, meeting all core requirements.
